title: feat(console): one app icon everywhere — an automatic solid colour for an app that declares none, no gradients on Home
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuHpGKAMhNVa11DUBYdEDSaq)_

Fixes #36157

repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgXNXwc6aap2K3v32WF

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

Nothing `@object-ui/app-shell` exports changes: `AppMark`, `appTileColors`, `launcherTile`, `HomeAppsStrip` and `productBlocks` are not on its entry, and the exported `AppSwitcher` keeps its props. No `packages/spec` path is touched; the palette is read from the existing `OBJECT_COLORS` export, and the tile classes from the existing `OBJECT_COLOR_TILE_CLASS` export of `@object-ui/components`.

## What changes

The rule, from the card: one app is one icon and one colour everywhere.

1. **One helper decides the face.** `appTileFace(app)` in `layout/appTileColors.ts` answers for every place an app's icon is drawn: a hex `branding.primaryColor` gives the declared tile (unchanged), and otherwise the app gets an automatic palette colour. A declared `branding.logo` is still drawn first by each surface, unchanged. `AppMark` (the app pill, every switcher row, the phone's app pill and app list, the phone drawer header, Studio's package chip) and Home's 56 px launcher tile both draw that face, so Home no longer carries its own copy of the rule.
2. **An app with no logo and no hex colour gets a solid colour.** One name from the objects' palette without its neutral `gray`, in the palette's order: blue, teal, green, amber, orange, red, pink, purple (`AUTO_TILE_COLORS`). The pick, `autoTileColor(name)`: djb2 over the app's `name` (start 5381, `hash = (hash << 5) + hash + charCode`, then `hash & hash` to keep a signed 32-bit integer), absolute value, modulo 8 — the repo's `simpleHash` form. It is computed at display time and never written back. The square uses `OBJECT_COLOR_TILE_CLASS` with a white glyph, the object tile's light and dark values (their white-glyph contrast is pinned by #35985's test).
3. **No gradients.** Home's tiles draw the solid face. `launcherTile.ts`'s ten-gradient table and `launcherIconGradient` are deleted. The `tile-grid` page block, which draws Home's tile, takes `launcherTileColorClasses(href || label)`: the same palette and the same pick, keyed as its gradient was (seat ruling on the claim, F1).
4. **The command palette's "Switch app" items** draw the app's `AppMark` (logo or square) instead of a bare line icon (seat ruling, F2). `AppMark`'s glyph size is now important (`size-3.5!` / `size-4!`) so a host row's `[&_svg]` sizing cannot grow it.
5. **Buttons are unchanged.** Only a declared `branding` reaches `AppShell`'s theme, so an app without a `primaryColor` keeps the platform's default `--primary`.
6. App and object colours may coincide, and two apps may share a colour; nothing separates them (card item 5).

Left alone, as the claim says: the avatar menu's hidden-app rows (line icons beside the other account items, F3) and `AppCard` (no mount site and not exported, F5).

Correction to the card's unchecked note: `#7C3AED` (purple) is HotCRM's **Expenses** app's primary colour. The Sales app, `crm_enterprise`, declares `#EA580C` (orange) with its logo, so its orange buttons are what it declares.

## Why

An app that declared neither a logo nor a colour (every AI-built app, and the `create-objectstack` blank template's `blank_main_app`) was drawn on one of ten gradients on Home and on a neutral grey square in the app menu, so one app looked like two. The maintainer agreed: an automatic solid colour, the same everywhere, no gradients on Home, and app/object colour collisions are not handled.

Who changes: only apps with no logo and no hex colour. Every HotCRM app and every repo example or platform app declares a `primaryColor` (or a logo) and draws as before.

| App | Declares | Before (Home / menu) | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| HotCRM Sales `crm_enterprise` | logo + `#EA580C` | logo | logo |
| HotCRM Service / O2C / PSA / Expenses / Marketing | own hex colour | that colour | that colour |
| `showcase_app`, `setup`, `account`, `studio`, `crm_app`, `todo_app` | hex colour (todo also a logo) | that colour / logo | unchanged |
| `blank_main_app` (blank template) | nothing | pink→rose gradient / grey | purple |
| an AI-built app such as `meeting_notes` / `crm_customer_management` | nothing | gradient / grey | pink / orange |

## Verification

- Unit (new top-level `describe`s in the existing harness files, per the ruling that a new pin joins the component's shared file):
  - `AppSwitcher.appIdentity-12201.test.tsx`: `AUTO_TILE_COLORS` is `OBJECT_COLORS` without `gray`, in order; the pick is pinned name by name (an empty name, an ASCII name, a CJK name whose hash is negative, a long name); `appTileFace` ladder (declared hex, non-hex → automatic, no name → neutral); the pill and its switcher row draw the same colour. Flipped pin: the old "neutral tile" control is now the automatic colour.
  - `HomeAppsStrip.branding-27386.test.tsx`: no declared colour → the palette square, no gradient class; Home's tile and `AppMark` give the same face for the same app. Flipped pin: the old "keeps the name-keyed gradient" case.
  - `ConsoleLayout.appBrandingLogo-10827.test.tsx` (real `AppShell`): an undeclared app's pill is automatic while `--brand-primary`, `--primary` and `--sidebar-primary` stay unset; control: a declared colour sets them.
  - `CommandPalette.launcherHiddenApps-26838.test.tsx`: a "Switch app" item draws a declared tile, a logo and an automatic tile.
  - `productBlocks-12197.test.tsx`: a `tile-grid` tile is the palette square keyed by its `href`, no gradient.
- Local, against main `146b6f9b`: the five files above pass; every ui test file that imports or names `AppMark`, `AppSwitcher`, `HomeAppsStrip`, `PhoneAppList`, `CommandPalette`, `productBlocks`, `launcherTile`, `PackageSwitcher`, `app-launcher-renderer` or `appTileColors` (154 files, 1,395 tests) pass; `tsc --noEmit` for `@object-ui/app-shell` clean; `eslint` on the changed files 0 errors.
- Browser: HotCRM main `6090c83` via `objectstack dev`, with `primaryColor` removed locally (not committed) from Marketing (`crm_marketing` → blue) and Expenses (`crm_expenses` → purple) so they declare nothing; console `vite` from this branch. 1440 and 375, light and dark, before and after: Home, the app menu, the ⌘K "Switch app" group, the phone app list and the phone app pill. Before: both apps are gradients on Home and grey in the menu. After: the same solid colour with a white glyph in every place; Sales keeps its logo, the four declared apps their colours. Shots are in the project thread's evidence folder (`build-seat1/36157/`).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- #36112 writes a new desktop app menu: it gets this rule by drawing `AppMark`.

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed. (not touched)
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
